note: Hard B, root reading: base.json is null (a lineage root has no mother), so the declared difference is against the framework stock cfg -- the only base a root can have. This file was COMPUTED from this recipe's own resolved cfg (rl_exp/tools/pipeline/emit_diff_declaration.py): the paths are the leaves that differ from stock and the element named under each group is the one that moved them in the replay, so the paths here cannot disagree with the build. The why strings are TODO until an author writes them: hard B compares paths, not prose, so an unwritten reason is a review item rather than a wrong claim.

lizard2_robot.why: The family's asset primitive, read from the frozen yaml (lizard2_recipe.lizard2_robot): assets/lizard2/lizard2.usda, base_link, the 30-joint init state including `.*_hip_joint`, three implicit-PD actuator groups, soft_joint_pos_limit_factor=0.95. The stock cfg scenes a framework demo articulation, so prim_path/spawn/init_state/actuators/class_type differ wholesale -- each of these paths is the robot's identity, not a tuning choice. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_flat_ground.why: Flat ground is the whole point of v1: terrain_type plane, no generator, and no height scanner (it would scan a constant). The stock velocity cfg builds rough terrain AND attaches a scanner, which is why these three paths are this element's and not the wiring's. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_proprio_obs.why: One group of seven proprio terms: height_scan removed (the stock registers it for the rough task) and enable_corruption off -- observation noise is a randomization like any other, so it is switched off rather than left at the stock default. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_actions.why: The deployed two-group action split (legs 20 / spine 10) replaces the stock single joint_pos over all joints. v1's yaml declares no action.joints, so the group membership is the class default while the scales come from the yaml -- a reference run on a different action interface could not answer a question about this robot as deployed. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_no_dr.why: Every randomization event the framework base registers, named and removed (physics_material, add_base_mass, base_com, base_external_force_torque, push_robot); two of those are not c_k-gated at all, so deleting the c_k clock alone would leave them at full strength forever. The two events that must stay stay: reset_base and reset_robot_joints have their ranges zeroed axis by axis (whatever axes the base declares) so the spawn is a deterministic pose rather than a hidden randomization -- and reset_robot_joints is, in this IsaacLab, the only writer of joint state at reset, so deleting it would respawn each env carrying the stale pose of the episode before (verified by rl_exp/tools/verify/reset_check.py). (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_rewards.why: The v1 reward set from the frozen yaml: the exp tracking kernel replaced by the symmetric Miki kernel, ang_vel_xy_l2/dof_acc_l2/feet_air_time/flat_orientation_l2/dof_pos_limits removed BY NAME (not by omission -- a framework base that re-registers one shows up here), undesired_contacts repointed at the yaml's body list, and belly_contact_force added as a continuous contact-force penalty (no dead zone, so the gradient survives touchdown). (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_contact_gate.why: The whole termination set, two ways to be down on a flat plane: `base_contact` is the framework term narrowed to the yaml's base body and threshold (the torso touching the ground = lying down), and `head_contact` is the framework's own `illegal_contact` pointed at the yaml's front -chain patterns (`chest_.*`, `neck_.*`) with the SAME 1.0 N, so the guard adds no kernel and leaves no second number to reason about. It is a CONTACT gate rather than a load criterion on purpose: the sibling line's v1 lost its whole run to a policy that bore weight on its neck in 66% of frames -- long enough to wreck the gait, never long enough to trip a dwell-based load rule -- and a contact gate cannot be averaged out. The dwell question is answered by the contact sensor's own history window (3 frames) instead of an added timer, which is why that line's dwell-capable kernel is not copied here: it implements a dwell this line does not declare. Added 2026-09-22 as a pre-training revision (v1 untrained), so both entries are this revision's. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_no_curriculum.why: terrain_levels is the framework base's only curriculum term and this line has no curriculum at all (both kinds declare False in the recipe table); the staged speed and terrain curricula are other lines' code and do not exist here. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

lizard2_velocity_command.why: The command RANGE landed exactly as the yaml wrote it: lin_vel_x [0.0, 3.0] m/s with lin_vel_y and ang_vel_z fixed at 0.0 (a range, not a fixed speed; widened from 0-2 to 0-3 before training so the top carries headroom past the sibling line's 3.0). heading_command and rel_standing_envs are off explicitly because either can rewrite the issued command at runtime -- heading_command would recompute ang_vel_z from the heading error, and rel_standing_envs would zero a fraction of envs while they still collect tracking reward. The startup probe reads the issued tensor rather than trusting this element. Note for readers of the verdict: the actuator estimate puts 3 m/s beyond the hip's torque budget, so the top of this window is measured by the capability curve (plan hard precondition 4), not assumed reachable. (compared against the framework stock cfg, base.json = null: a lineage root)

agent.why: The agent is a class, not a declaration: these entries carry a reason and no element name.

allowed.experiment_name: lizard2_v1 -- this version's own log directory (versioning.mdc A: one version, one log dir). Inheriting the base's lizard_baseline_v1 would file two different robots' runs under one name, and every record keyed by that name would be ambiguous.
allowed.max_iterations: 10000 -- declared as what is actually intended, not the base's 3000 (baseline v1's recorded run was cut short by its own budget). Same budget as the other line's v2 for the same reason: a command RANGE means two commands per 20 s episode, and this skeleton's learning curve is unknown. Acceptance lines live in PLAN.md.
allowed.num_steps_per_env: set by Lizard2PPORunnerCfg, inherited unchanged from LizardBaselinePPORunnerCfg (the lizard baseline v1 recipe: the framework's own velocity-task PPO hyperparameters, explicitly not the paper S1 recipe nor the three-encoder model, both tuned for a 381-dim three-group observation at 4096 envs). The stock OnPolicyRunnerCfg leaves this leaf unset, which is why the difference appears here at all -- this version changes the skeleton, not the optimizer. Consequence: a PPO hyperparameter edit in the baseline runner moves this family too; accepted because the two are meant to be the same recipe, and the dependency is a code import visible in the edit.
